gloss: gidayū; narrative chanting for bunraku puppet theater

definitions.gloss: gidayū; narrative chanting for bunraku puppet theater
definitions.explanation: A style of dramatic narrative chanting accompanied by shamisen, developed in the late 17th century by Takemoto Gidayū. It is the vocal element of bunraku puppet theater and is also performed independently as a concert form.

examples.japanese: {義太夫|ぎだゆう}を{習|なら}っている。
{文楽|ぶんらく}では{義太夫|ぎだゆう}が{物語|ものがたり}を{語|かた}る。
examples.english: In bunraku, the gidayū narrator tells the story.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}から{義太夫|ぎだゆう}の{語|かた}り{手|て}として{活動|かつどう}してきた。
examples.english: My grandfather has worked as a gidayū chanter since he was young.

notes:
Short for {義太夫節|ぎだゆうぶし}, named after the 17th-century chanter {竹本義太夫|たけもとぎだゆう}. Functions both as the vocal narration of {文楽|ぶんらく} (bunraku puppet theater) and as an independent classical art form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {義太夫|ぎだゆう}を{語|かた}る: to perform gidayū
- {義太夫|ぎだゆう}{節|ぶし}: the full name of the genre
- {女|おんな}{義太夫|ぎだゆう}: female gidayū performance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {長唄|ながうた}: nagauta — shamisen song style for kabuki
- {浄瑠璃|じょうるり}: jōruri — the broader genre of narrative chanting that gidayū belongs to
